details:
**Diego Maradona lying in state**
Argentina's most famous footballer, who led the national team to the 1986 World Cup title, died in November 2020. His coffin lay in state at the Casa Rosada, the presidential palace in Buenos Aires, where huge crowds of mourners gathered and clashed with police.

**Legalization of abortion (2020)**
In December 2020, Argentina's Congress legalized elective abortion up to the 14th week of pregnancy, after a similar bill had failed in the Senate in 2018. It made Argentina the largest country in Latin America to legalize abortion at the time.

**Green handkerchiefs**
The green scarves (pañuelos verdes) worn by Argentine activists campaigning for legal, safe, and free abortion. The symbol, inspired by the white headscarves of the Mothers of the Plaza de Mayo, spread across Latin America as the "green wave" of abortion-rights movements.

**Alberto Fernández**
The Peronist president of Argentina from 2019 to 2023, who championed the abortion legalization bill. Soon after taking office he traveled to the Vatican to meet Pope Francis, seeking support in Argentina's debt negotiations.

**Pope Francis**
Born Jorge Mario Bergoglio in Buenos Aires, he was Archbishop of Buenos Aires before becoming the first Latin American pope in 2013. He is Argentina's most famous native son in religious affairs and died in 2025.

**2020 wealth tax on the richest citizens**
In late 2020, Argentina passed a one-time "solidarity contribution" levied on roughly 12,000 people with fortunes above 200 million pesos to fund the country's COVID-19 response. Rates on domestic assets ranged up to about 3.5 percent.

**2001 debt default**
At the height of a severe economic crisis in late 2001, Argentina defaulted on about 100 billion dollars of sovereign debt, then the largest default in history. The crisis brought bank withdrawal limits (the corralito), riots, and a rapid succession of presidents.

**Paul Singer and NML Capital**
Singer's hedge fund, Elliott Management, through its subsidiary NML Capital, bought defaulted Argentine bonds cheaply and refused restructuring deals, suing for full repayment. These "holdout" or "vulture fund" creditors won a large settlement in 2016 under President Mauricio Macri.

**ARA Libertad**
An Argentine navy training frigate that was detained at the port of Tema in Ghana in 2012 at the request of NML Capital, which sought to seize it as payment for defaulted debt. It was released after an international tribunal on the law of the sea ordered Ghana to let it go.

**Buenos Aires**
The capital and largest city of Argentina, located on the Río de la Plata. It is home to the Casa Rosada and the Plaza de Mayo, the main site of Argentine political protest.

**Cristina Fernández de Kirchner**
Argentina's president from 2007 to 2015 and later vice president under Alberto Fernández. She survived an assassination attempt in 2022 when a gun aimed at her failed to fire, and that same year was convicted of fraud related to public works contracts.

**Javier Milei**
The libertarian economist elected president of Argentina in 2023, who campaigned while brandishing a chainsaw to symbolize slashing government spending. He pursued drastic austerity to fight the country's very high inflation.

**Lionel Messi and the 2022 World Cup**
Argentina's star forward, who captained the national team to victory over France in the 2022 World Cup final in Qatar. It was Argentina's third World Cup title and its first since Maradona's 1986 triumph.
